claims.text: Conventional metal rollers and guide plates directly exposed to molten aluminum are prone to rapid corrosion.
A dense, sintered Al2O3 coating can be applied to conventional metal parts using surface or interface engineering techniques.
Hot dip aluminum plating exposes equipment parts to molten aluminum at approximately 660 degrees Celsius or above.
A sintered alumina layer can form a dense and continuous barrier on the metal substrate.
The alumina barrier prevents direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying metal.
Alumina has an extremely high melting point relative to the hot dip aluminum plating temperature.
Alumina is chemically inert with respect to molten aluminum.
The alumina coating resists thermal degradation during exposure to molten aluminum.
The alumina coating resists chemical attack by molten aluminum.
Resistance to thermal degradation and chemical attack reduces oxidation and erosion of the underlying metal.
Alumina-coated components will have a significantly lower erosion rate than uncoated components.
Alumina-coated components will undergo less chemical degradation than uncoated components.
Reduced erosion and chemical degradation will extend the operational lifetime of plating equipment.
Uncoated metal parts rapidly corrode and erode in direct contact with high-temperature molten aluminum.
Rapid corrosion of uncoated parts necessitates frequent replacement.
Protective effectiveness depends on coating density and adhesion quality.
Protective effectiveness depends on the thermal and mechanical stresses encountered in operation.
Poor coating quality, delamination, fracture, or extreme operating conditions can reduce the protective effect.
